title: Loop a printed self-adhesive baggage tag through a suitcase handle and seal it
instruction: Attach the printed baggage tag securely to the suitcase's long-side handle, with the barcode facing out. Its back is self-adhesive and sticks only to itself: loop it through the handle, lay one strand over the other with the backs together and press them, then release the tag and withdraw both arms.
context: At self-service bag drop, a passenger pulls the printed tag from the outlet and seals it around the bag handle before handing the suitcase over. The physical challenge is feeding a flexible strip through the closed handle, receiving the partly hidden end, and bringing the correct faces together without losing the loop. Printing is already complete; barcode reading is outside the task; no flight booking or baggage transport is simulated.
setup: Official bimanual YAM station, one overhead and two wrist cameras, fixed layout. A small hard-shell suitcase (approximately 450 x 178 x 334 mm in its side-standing orientation) is supported on a scale, its existing long-side strap handle upwards with approximately 30 mm central clearance. A 460 x 145 mm terminal/presenter stands to its right; a 21 mm-high hollow channel and single outlet retain one already printed thermal self-tag (POS Supply AIR-SLFTAG21RL-SS, 2 x 21 in / 51 x 533 mm, printed front, whole back self-only adhesive as on Eezeetags linerless tags), with approximately 90 mm protruding. The entire strip exists at reset. No auxiliary grip tabs or pre-threading. README and task.py provide all positions, dimensions and materials; PRESENTER.md gives a low-cost passive reconstruction so an operational airport kiosk is not needed.
scoring: Current outcome tiers, not cumulative or peak score. All nonzero scores require the complete, intact label to be out of the outlet, the tag's adhesive back physically pressed onto another part of its own back and sealed with at least 600 mm² overlap, so that the sealed tag forms a closed loop around the actual handle, and the printed barcode face exposed outwards above the shell. An inward-facing or hidden barcode fails this prerequisite; barcode decoding is not evaluated. 0 otherwise, including extraction alone, loose threading, a loop beside the handle, or broken paper/connection. 0.75 for that intact linked seal; 0.85 once both grippers are open and clear and the loop remains within 5 mm of its hold-start position for 0.25 seconds; 1.0 after all prerequisites and that released stable state persist for at least 2 seconds. Real trials use video/photos and a ruler: at least 75 mm hand clearance and no corner drifting more than 5 mm from its position at the start of the hold. Exact hand assignment, handle lifting and arm home pose are not scored. Simulator geometry and adhesion tolerances are specified separately in README and tag_closure.py.
run_limit: 4,800 control steps at 20 Hz (240 simulated seconds).
reset_notes: Replace the used printed label, load its trailing end into the presenter with 90 mm protruding, and reset both arms. Use self-bonding cold-seal luggage stock; no liner-removal step is omitted. Fixed seed 42, object_jitter=0.
fidelity: 14 hinged colliding panels approximate the 533 x 51 mm, 4.8 g tag; bending EI 6.8e-5 N m2 from Clark 60 (patent range), air drag as linear damping. The whole back bonds only back to back, never to case, handle or grippers: a seal needs >=0.5 N on both backs for 0.4 s from native PhysX contacts, then a breakable joint forms at the current pose. Force/dwell, break limits and friction are tuning. Chemistry and peel omitted. Handle is a rigid spring proxy.
scores: Rev3 continuous scripted demo: 1.0, 3208 control steps / 160.4 simulated seconds, seal at 1.16 N, 3.95 seconds of released stability. Dream-1-beta (1,000 control steps): 0.0.
